subject: pet tarantulas
one_liner: Commission-free investing for tarantulas, who are long-term holders by temperament and have not moved since March.
brand_voice_notes: Retail-brokerage confidence applied to an animal that sits still for nine days at a time. Treat stillness as conviction, molting as a scheduled trading halt, and urticating hairs as a risk-management feature. Never acknowledge that a spider cannot read a chart. Owners are referred to as 'the custodian'.

hero.h1: Your tarantula has held the same position for eleven days. Molt makes it count.
hero.sub: Commission-free trading in crickets, dubia roaches and substrate futures. Orders execute when your spider moves. Your spider rarely moves. Our compliance team calls this conviction.

features.title: Eight-leg order routing
features.blurb: Each leg places one order. A Chilean rose hair crossing her enclosure can submit eight trades before she reaches the water dish, and we route every one of them, including the ones she did not mean.

features.title: Premolt trading halt
features.blurb: When your tarantula flips onto her back and stops eating, Molt freezes the account for three to six weeks. Custodians tend to panic here. Compliance has seen it 41,000 times and recommends touching nothing, the spider included.

features.title: Burrow mode
features.blurb: Hides the portfolio under four inches of coco fiber so neither you nor the spider can check it daily. Returns rose 3% in our internal study, which had one participant, a Goliath birdeater named Doug.

demo_screen_concept: A mobile brokerage home screen for Gertrude, a Chilean rose hair. A large portfolio balance in cricket-equivalents with a silk-thread sparkline and range tabs (1D, 1W, 1 MOLT, 25Y). A holdings list of tickers: CRKT crickets, DUBI dubia roaches, MEAL mealworms, COCO substrate futures, H2O water dish. Tapping a ticker opens an order sheet; placing an order sets it to 'Awaiting leg movement' with an eight-leg meter that fills only when you press 'Nudge enclosure'. A Burrow Mode toggle blurs every balance, and a Molt Calendar tab shows the next scheduled trading halt.

design_direction.style: Claymorphic neo-brokerage, terrarium daylight mode. A friendly retail trading app rendered in soft inflated clay: rounded cards with layered soft shadows, a clay phone mockup in the hero, pill buttons that squish on press. Staged inside a vivarium: pale coco-substrate ground, silk threads, and a molted skin left behind every card. Explicitly absent, because the last seven entries used them: LCD greens, parts diagrams, warning boxes, plum buttons, rhumb lines, cartouches, scale bars, wax seals, acorn marks, dot maps, status-dot lists, terminal panels, name tags, punch cards, thermal tickets, matte dark mode, lime LEDs, conflict markers, gutter stripes, data strips, viewfinder brackets, infrared. Also absent: dark backgrounds, glassmorphism, neon, purple gradients, gradients behind body text. Four motifs carry the page. (1) The silk thread: every chart is a single 2px silk-white line with a darker ink shadow and tiny dewdrop nodes at data points, hung from a short vertical anchor thread. (2) The leg meter: eight small rounded bars in two rows of four, used for order status, feature numbering and pricing tier strength. (3) The exuvia: cards carry a dashed, slightly offset and rotated ghost outline behind them, like a shed skin left on the substrate. (4) The red knee: Mexican red-knee orange #E0601C is rationed to the primary CTA, the highlighted tier and the 'molt imminent' chip. Gains use a moss green; losses use bruised brown, always with an arrow glyph. Corners 28px on cards, 999px on buttons. Shadows are clay stacks: a soft outer drop plus an inner highlight, never hard lines.
design_direction.archetype: App Store style landing: hero with clay device mockup, features, reviews, pricing, download CTAs
design_direction.motion_vocab: Slow, spider-paced. Buttons squish to scale 0.94 on press with a spring return. The hero sparkline draws itself over 1.6s like a thread being laid. Leg-meter bars fill one at a time with a 90ms stagger. Everything else holds still for a long, uncomfortable time. prefers-reduced-motion disables all of it.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Two columns on desktop. Left: Calistoga h1 at clamp(40px, 5.4vw, 72px), sub in Inter 19px, red-knee pill CTA plus a secondary 'Open the demo' clay pill, then a row of fake app-store rating chips. Right: a clay phone mockup tilted 4 degrees, showing Gertrude's balance and a silk sparkline, hung from a thin silk thread anchored to the top of the viewport. A dashed exuvia outline of the phone sits behind it, offset 14px and rotated -3 degrees. Stacks to one column under 900px with the phone below the copy.
